title: Playing nightly in the District for tips and pay
summary: After a question on marriage, Picou describes eight-to-four shifts at a dollar and a quarter, no dancing, requests, and a $50 tip.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How old were you when you got married now, Paul?
That's where I started smelling myself.

Smelling myself. Smelling myself. Smelling myself. You know? You're just getting to their heart. Oh, you know that. You must have been crying. Oh, you know that. You know that. You know that. You know that. Because you're a young man. You know that. And during the time you were married, during that time,
you were working in the district for a long time. Oh, yes, indeed. I used to work in the district.

Where we used to go at eight o'clock. And play from eight to four. How about you think? Dollar and a quarter a night. Wow. You know that's like a thing. Dollar and a quarter a night. Was that like in a night club? Yeah. Uh-huh. Yeah. I forgot his name.
Did people dance there? No, not much dance.
Not much dance. Not much dance. Not much dance.
But ask for the numbers that they want. Yeah. We had to play them.
Yeah, do you remember the numbers they used to ask for? No. None of them, huh? Just popular songs or... Yeah, old songs. The old songs. Yeah, old songs. Yeah, old songs.
Yeah, old songs. Yeah, old songs. Yeah, old songs. Yeah, old songs.
Yeah, old songs. But you don't remember the names of those songs, huh? No, no. I don't know.
You don't remember songs like The Man Who Broke The Bank at Monte Carlo? No, no, no. No, they didn't play those here at all, no? Uh-huh. Or did you just play for the customers?
Customers come in and have a drink?
Customers. Customers. Uh-huh. Now, the customers used to come from the... Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh.

Uh-huh. They come away. And it's all white. Yeah. And they come from away. They will ask us the player number. The fellow will come with a $10 bill, give you that, just like he'd give you a liquor. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. But with half a dollar and a quarter. You understand? Yeah. Remember that number? And we played it. And it was heat to shine on my clarinet with that. He gave us a $50 bill. Oh, Lord, we'll never forget that. $50. How many were in the band about that? Oh, Lord. We never did forget that. How many people were in the band to split that up? How many? Four. Four. Four. What did you have? The guitar and bass? Or did you use the piano? Sometimes the piano.
